Appreciate the clarity. Attached is an initial MAP + benchmarking plan (nova_map_plan_v1.xlsx). High-level items we propose:

1) Test matrix
- Concurrency: 10, 25, 50, 100 sessions
- Sequence lengths: 12 tokens (short turn), 64 tokens (typical), 256 tokens (long turn)
- Model variants: rw-std-7b (baseline quality), rw-q4-7b (quantized perf), rw-llm-3.5-compat (lower-latency, slightly lower qual)

2) Metrics captured
- P50/P95/P99 latency per token and per response
- Throughput measured as tokens/sec and responses/min
- TTFT distribution (cold vs warm cache)
- Error rate and rate-limited responses

3) Environment & routing
- Tests run in us-west region against Dedicated staging cluster (matching the planned pilot topology)
- Route slow-fallback policy enabled to measure graceful degradation

4) Schedule / close timeline
- 7/28–7/30: MAP review + confirm variants and dataset (you provide 3 representative prompt sets)
- 7/31–8/02: Benchmark runs (automated harness)
- 8/03: Results review & recommendation (this will include CSV of raw metrics)
- 8/04–8/10: Procurement + SOC2 evidence exchange; target pilot start 8/12

Notes: We expect the quantized variant (rw-q4-7b) to give ~30–40% token-cost reduction with modest TTFT improvements, but some quality degradation on medically precise prompts. The 3.5-compat variant will likely hit the lowest P95 latency at the cost of hallucination risk for rare queries.

Hi all —

I ran a preliminary harness outline and pushed test configs to the shared Drive (see link). A few technical clarifications before we start:

- Concurrency model: we will simulate 50 concurrent sessions using realistic think times derived from your sample traces (please upload 48–72 hours of logs).
- KV cache warm vs cold: we should run both; warm cache expected to reduce TTFT by ~12–20% depending on variant.
- Measurement: we capture per-token GPU time (kernel-level), queue time, and serialization overhead.

Candidate model variants (shortlisted):
- rw-std-7b (float16) — highest quality; P95 expect ~420–650ms at 50 concurrency depending on seq length
- rw-q4-7b (int8/quant) — faster, ~280–420ms P95; ~30% fewer tokens billed; some rare QA drops on long-context clinical cases
- rw-lite-3.5c — optimized for latency; P95 ~180–300ms but quality delta vs rw-std-7b TBD on your prompts

I will run 3 passes (short, typical, long) and export raw CSVs. If NovaHealth wants we can also run a small A/B quality eval on a 200-prompt holdout set.

Laura
